statement: The repository publishes a machine-readable compatibility matrix generated from live external-client scenarios against named driver versions and SQL features; each supported cell has a test receipt, unsupported cells are explicit, and a release cannot silently regress a supported cell. Verified at HEAD 761dc17c7: real-client compatibility tests exist (test/compatibility/pgwire-client-compat.test.js with pg and psql, postgres:16 baselines) plus a test-coverage index, but no machine-readable supported/unsupported feature matrix is generated from receipts; PostgreSQL compatibility is Community/AGPL scope per edition-matrix.md.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn an independent verifier before audit and handoff and record its stable evidence id.

The pgwire runtime and existing compatibility tests remain the owners of wire behavior; this Quest adds the matrix generation and regression gate over their receipts. No second compatibility claim surface.

The matrix is generated from test receipts, not hand-maintained prose. Initial clients: Node pg, psql, and one additional pilot-relevant driver selected from actual customer discovery; do not claim an ORM merely because its underlying driver connects. Initial dimensions: startup/TLS/authentication, simple and extended query, parameter types, transactions, DDL, inserts/updates/deletes, result types, errors, connection pooling, prepared statements, cancellation behavior, and lifecycle SQL permissions.
A release cannot silently regress a supported cell: the matrix diff is checked in the release process and unsupported cells are explicit rather than absent.
Wrong-password, wrong-CA, and unsupported-SQL attacks remain red; hand-editing the matrix without receipts or deleting a supported cell's test must fail the gate.
